column1: # Fixture miss table for harness/test-recall-runner.sh (bead tla-1sh7.6).
# This file pins the FORMAT recall/MISSES.tsv uses. It is not the corpus; the
# real table is bead tla-1sh7.3's, carries 30 rows, and is reached by one
# live row at the end of the suite rather than by the fixture cases.
# Rows are tab-delimited and carry the literal first field MISS, so prose in
# this file can never be read as data. Four fields, in order:
#   1  marker       the literal MISS
#   2  rep id       a REP row in REPS.tsv beside this file
#   3  wrong        the wrong answer, as TLA+, verbatim
#   4  explanation  what that answer says
# WHAT EACH ROW IS FOR, since this is a fixture and not a corpus:
#   R001  the answer every other part of the suite already submits as its
#         wrong one, so the layer rides on a value the fixture has measured.
#         It is also the row the whitespace rows aim at: the suite submits
#         the same mistake spaced three ways and requires all three to reach
#         this row, and the exact-match mutant requires two of them to stop.
#   R002  a second rep, so a row firing is not one rep's accident.
# NO ROW FOR `[Tracks -> Wagons]`, WHICH IS DELIBERATE. That is case C004, a
# wrong answer to R001 that this table has nothing to say about, and it is
# how the suite reaches the path 90 of the 120 real reps take. A table that
# answered every fixture case would leave that path untested.
# FIELD 4 SAYS WHAT THE WRONG ANSWER IS, NOT WHAT TO WRITE INSTEAD, which is
# the register recall/MISSES.tsv sets and the reason it can be printed under
# two values that already show the right answer.
MISS
column4: That's one parking, and what it gives back for every wagon is the whole set of tracks rather than a single track.

column1: MISS
column4: That parks every wagon on the second track. It is a parking of the right shape standing in the wrong place.
